explanation.en: Form IV prefixes a hamza: أَفْعَلَ يُفْعِلُ, masdar إِفْعَال. It is usually causative/transitive: رَجَعَ (to return, intransitive) → أَرْجَعَ (to give something back). أَرَادَ (to want) is Form IV of ر-و-د. Its hamza is hamzat qat' — written with the seat (أ) and never dropping: قَالَ وَأَرَادَ, unlike the wasl of Form I imperatives.

examples.en: I returned the book to the library.

why.en: رَجَعَ is intransitive ("to come back"); giving something back needs the Form IV causative أَرْجَعَ.
Form IV takes hamzat qat' — spell it أَرَادَ, never اراد. In careful writing the hamza is not optional.
